facts: HMS Wager was wrecked off the coast of Patagonia in 1741 during a British naval expedition.
The survivors split: one group under Captain David Cheap stayed; another, led by the gunner John Bulkeley, sailed a lengthened boat out and reached Brazil.
Bulkeley's men and the later returnees under Cheap and midshipman John Byron gave different accounts of what happened.
Each account blamed the other side's conduct, including mutiny and the killing of a sailor.
Back in England the Admiralty held a court martial about the loss of the ship; Cheap was found to have done his duty, one officer was reprimanded, and the mutiny was not prosecuted.
Grann's point is that the Admiralty preferred not to punish anyone, and different survivors told incompatible stories.

Wager was part of Anson's squadron; Bulkeley's group crossed the Strait of Magellan to Brazil; Cheap shot a seaman; Bulkeley's journal printed 1743; Byron's narrative 1768; four men of Cheap's party reached Chile.
scene_details: a wrecked ship on a Patagonian coast

tension: Survivors from the same wreck arrive home with accounts that blame each other.
opening_idea: Open on the court martial: two groups of survivors from one shipwreck, and incompatible stories.

lessons.idea: When two sides describe the same event differently, ask what each side gains from its version.
lessons.anchor: Bulkeley's and Byron's accounts of the wreck differed

reflect_final: Think of a recent disagreement: what would the other person's version say about what happened, and what would they gain from it?

use_cases.situation: Two team members report the same incident differently.
use_cases.move: Ask each for what they saw and what they did, separately, before judging.

use_cases.situation: Siblings remember a family event differently.
use_cases.move: Say you would like to hear their version first.

use_cases.situation: You hear one side of a friend's falling out.
use_cases.move: Say you would like to hear more before taking a position.

pocket_idea: Wager survivors told incompatible stories of one wreck: before judging, ask what each version gains the teller.

conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: In 1741 HMS Wager was wrecked off Patagonia. One group of survivors, led by gunner John Bulkeley, sailed to Brazil. Others, including Captain Cheap and John Byron, returned later by a different route. Back in England, each group's account blamed the other, and the Admiralty held a court martial that ended without punishing the mutiny. David Grann tells this in The Wager.
